gen_risks.description: Delay in recruiting required specialist staff (accountant, environmental, gender‑based violence, etc.) within the one‑month deadline.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop an accelerated recruitment plan, use temporary contracts, and monitor hiring milestones weekly.
gen_risks.evidence: CEMAC Financing Agreement: appoint, assign, or recruit an accountant, environmental specialist, gender‑based violence consultant not later than one month after Effective Date.

gen_risks.description: Failure to customize accounting software for the project within three months of effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage an IT vendor before project start, allocate dedicated budget, and set clear deliverable dates with penalties for delay.
gen_risks.evidence: CEMAC Financing Agreement: customize existing accounting software no later than three months after the Effective Date.

gen_risks.description: Procurement delays caused by weak market competition and limited contract management capacity in fragile settings.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire experienced procurement specialists, conduct early market engagement, and adopt flexible procurement methods approved by the Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement leading to community opposition and project delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Umbrella Stakeholder Engagement Plan, hold early consultations, and maintain transparent grievance redress mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential social risks are substantial and relate to inadequate stakeholder engagement to properly inform design and implementation.

gen_risks.description: Sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA/SH) risks arising from the expanded community health workforce.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct GBV/SEA risk assessments, recruit a dedicated GBV specialist, and train all staff on SEA/SH protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Overall project SEA/SH risks are substantial; increased presence of Community Health Workers may create concerns of sexual exploitation and abuse.

gen_risks.description: Political instability and conflict in Cameroon, CAR and Chad disrupting implementation and access to target areas.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop security risk assessments, flexible work plans, and contingency budgets; coordinate closely with UN/NGO security teams.
gen_risks.evidence: Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence, leading to large population displacements; Boko Haram attacks in Cameroon, unrest in CAR.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related events (floods, extreme heat) damaging health facilities and laboratory infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply green and resilient construction standards, elevate critical equipment, and incorporate climate‑risk assessments in design.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change contributed to at least 50 % of natural disasters; floods raise risk of cholera; project includes green and resilient approaches.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient domestic financing after project completion threatening sustainability of health security gains.
gen_risks.mitigation: Support development of medium‑term expenditure frameworks, track health‑security budgeting, and mobilize private‑sector partnerships.
gen_risks.evidence: Securing financial sustainability will be supported to integrate health security into national budgeting processes and domestic resource mobilization.

gen_risks.description: High turnover or capacity gaps in Project Implementation Units (PIUs) leading to implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer retention incentives, clear terms of reference, and continuous capacity‑building programmes for PIU staff.
gen_risks.evidence: PIUs will be led by a dedicated coordinator; staff recruitment and capacity building are required for effective implementation.

gen_risks.description: Laboratory biosafety incidents due to handling of high‑risk pathogens.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement strict biosafety and biosecurity SOPs, certify labs to international standards, and conduct regular training drills.
gen_risks.evidence: Laboratory Quality and Capacity subcomponent includes strengthening biosafety & biosecurity and establishing a quality management system.

gen_risks.description: Data interoperability failures across human, animal and environmental surveillance systems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a common data standards framework, deploy interoperable digital platforms, and provide joint training for data managers.
gen_risks.evidence: Subcomponent 2.1 aims to integrate OH data using an interoperable digital platform and develop dashboards for decision‑making.

gen_risks.description: Delay in establishing the Regional Coordination Committee (RCC) and formal MoUs with regional bodies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set a firm deadline of 30 days post‑effective date for MoU signing and monitor progress through quarterly reports.
gen_risks.evidence: CEMAC Financing Agreement: establish collaboration measures with WAHO no later than thirty days after the Effective Date.

gen_risks.description: Weak monitoring and evaluation leading to poor visibility of results and corrective actions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen M&E teams, adopt real‑time reporting tools, and conduct independent mid‑term evaluations.
gen_risks.evidence: PIUs are responsible for M&E of specific project activities and will report progress in accordance with the Results Framework.

gen_risks.description: Supply‑chain disruptions for medical countermeasures during an emergency response.
gen_risks.mitigation: Pre‑position essential stockpiles, develop logistics contingency plans, and establish agreements with regional suppliers.
gen_risks.evidence: Subcomponent 3.1 includes strengthening emergency logistics and stockpiling to ensure access to countermeasures.

gen_risks.description: Persistent gender gaps in epidemiology and veterinary training limiting workforce capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set gender‑balanced training targets, conduct outreach to women candidates, and provide flexible learning formats.
gen_risks.evidence: HeSP‑3 aims to close the gender gap in technical roles; women currently under‑represented in epidemiology and veterinary fields.

gen_risks.description: Delays in meeting legal conditions of effectiveness (e.g., adoption of Project Operations Manual).
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign a legal compliance officer to track all conditions and submit required documents ahead of deadlines.
gen_risks.evidence: Effectiveness conditions require the Recipient to prepare and adopt the Project Operations Manual within specified timeframes.

gen_risks.description: Bottlenecks in external audit procurement causing late financial reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Identify and pre‑qualify multiple audit firms, schedule audit timelines early, and maintain a backup auditor list.
gen_risks.evidence: Recipient must recruit an external auditor no later than six months after the Effective Date.

gen_risks.description: Resurgence of COVID‑19 or another pandemic disrupting training, travel and field activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop virtual training modules, enforce health safety protocols, and maintain flexible timelines for field work.
gen_risks.evidence: COVID‑19 pandemic exacerbated service delivery challenges; project includes digital platforms and remote training to mitigate such disruptions.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
